meta.title: Where Ontario’s rivers end
meta.method: Follow HydroRIVERS NEXT_DOWN links to the first configured receiving lake or river connection, otherwise the actual ocean outlet. Reveal distance is cumulative river-network length from that receiver. Provincial borders do not create outlets. Lake interior links are hidden. Percentages are shares of the mapped network length, including hidden internal lake connections, not land area, discharge, or all watercourses. HydroRIVERS models a generalized natural network; engineered diversions and every small stream are not represented.
meta.systemColorMethod: Colors follow connected receiving-water tributary networks. Named nested branches receive their own color throughout their upstream subnetwork; stable outlet-derived shades distinguish smaller unnamed networks.
meta.farthestDefinition: Maximum cumulative upstream network distance from the configured receiving water, across every headwater in the region.
meta.animationDistanceDefinition: One shared upstream network-distance threshold from every configured outlet; all outlets start together. Context paths outside Ontario use the same distances and are excluded from Ontario length totals.

last.label: Farthest upstream headwater
last.routeNote: Actual downstream HydroRIVERS links, including travel outside Ontario. Context route is excluded from Ontario length shares.
last.distanceDefinition: Maximum cumulative upstream network distance from the configured receiving water, across every headwater in the region.
last.routeDescription: Reaches Hudson Bay via the Rainy–Winnipeg–Nelson system

sources.title: Natural Earth 1:10m boundaries, land, lakes and river names

ontarioLongest.distanceDefinition: River-network distance from the Ontario receiving-water shore to the farthest headwater whose complete landward route remains in Ontario.

eligibility.definition: Complete coast/receiving-water-to-headwater route remains in Ontario within 1 km cartographic tolerance; only a receiving-water shoreline prefix may be excluded, never another province or country.
